game_info.title: MechWarrior / BattleTech Combat Rules
game_info.description: Comprehensive combat rules from BattleTech tabletop game and MechWarrior video game series
source_games: BattleTech tabletop game (FASA, Catalyst Game Labs)

resolution_system.description: BattleTech uses a 2D6 (two six-sided dice) resolution system. Roll 2D6 and add modifiers. If the total meets or exceeds the Target Number (TN), the check succeeds.

sequence_of_play.description: Each turn consists of several phases performed in order.

phases.name: Initiative Phase
phases.description: One player from each side rolls 2D6. Higher result wins Initiative for the turn. Re-roll ties.
phases.effects: Winner fires first but moves second. Loser moves first but fires second.

phases.name: Movement Phase
phases.description: Side that lost Initiative moves first. Side that won Initiative moves second.
phases.details: Each unit may move up to its Movement Points (MP) allowance. Movement is measured in hexes.

phases.name: Weapon Attack Phase
phases.description: Side that won Initiative fires first. Side that lost Initiative fires second.
phases.details: Each unit may fire weapons at targets within range. To-Hit Number depends on range, movement, and modifiers.

phases.name: Heat Phase
phases.description: Resolve heat accumulation and shutdown checks.
phases.details: If heat exceeds thresholds, roll 2D6 against Target Number to avoid shutdown.

phases.name: End Phase
phases.description: Cleanup and preparation for next turn.
phases.details: Remove temporary markers, check for mission objectives, advance turn counter.

movement_points.description: Each BattleMech has Walking Speed and Running (Sprint) Speed, measured in km/h. Converted to Movement Points (MP) for game purposes.
movement_points.restrictions: A unit may walk or run each turn, but not both. Running prevents weapon fire that turn due to recoil.

terrain_costs.description: Movement costs vary by terrain type. Each hex costs 1 MP plus a terrain modifier.

facing.description: Each unit has a facing direction. Changing facing costs 1 MP per 60 degrees of rotation.

arcs.side: Left or right, ±60 degrees from the side

facing.firing_penalties: Firing from the side or rear arc imposes penalties.

jump_jets.description: Jump jets allow vertical movement over obstacles and terrain, consuming additional MP and generating heat.
limitations: Limited by number of jump jets installed

to_hit_number.description: The To-Hit Number (THN) for a weapon attack is calculated as: THN = Base THN + Range Modifier + Movement Modifier + Terrain Modifier

hit_location_table.description: When a weapon attack hits a BattleMech, roll 2D6 to determine which location is struck.

armor_and_damage.description: Each BattleMech location has an Armor Value (AV) that absorbs incoming damage. Damage first reduces armor, then internal structure.
rules: Damage is first applied to the armor in the hit location
If damage exceeds armor value, excess is applied to internal structure
When internal structure is destroyed, the location is lost
Arms fall off when destroyed
Legs cause the mech to fall when destroyed
Head hits can kill the pilot
Center Torso destruction causes catastrophic explosion

critical_hits.description: When a BattleMech's armor in a location is reduced to zero, subsequent hits may cause critical hits.
rules: Roll to hit the location again
If it hits, check for critical hits on the critical hit slot map
Critical hits can destroy weapons, ammunition, heat sinks, cockpit, or engine
Destroying the engine causes the mech to shut down
Destroying the cockpit kills the pilot
Ammunition explosions deal massive damage and may cause chain reactions

physical_attacks.description: BattleMechs may perform physical attacks including punching, kicking, and ramming.
requirements: Attacker must be adjacent to the target
Attacker must be facing the target
physical_attacks.resolution: Roll 2D6 and add the attacker's Piloting Skill modifier. If the total meets or exceeds the Target Number, the attack hits.
physical_attacks.damage: Based on the attacker's tonnage and the type of attack.
effects: Kicking a damaged leg can cause the target to fall

heat_system.description: BattleMechs generate heat when firing weapons and using jump jets. Heat sinks dissipate heat each turn.
heat_sources: Jump jets (varies by number of jumps)

heat_sinks.standard: 1 heat point dissipated per sink per turn
heat_sinks.double: 2 heat points dissipated per sink per turn (takes twice the critical hit space)

shutdown_thresholds.description: At certain heat thresholds, the mech attempts an automatic shutdown.

shutdown_procedure.description: When heat reaches a threshold, roll 2D6 once during the Heat Phase.
rules: If the roll meets or exceeds the TN, the pilot avoids shutdown for that turn
If the roll fails, the mech shuts down and becomes immobile
At 30+ heat, shutdown is automatic and unavoidable
A shut-down mech cannot move or fire weapons but can still be targeted

heat_override.description: The player can override the automatic shutdown to continue fighting, but this risks internal damage and reactor explosion.

skills.description: Each MechWarrior has two primary skills: Gunnery and Piloting.
skills.gunnery: Affects weapon accuracy — higher Gunnery skill reduces the To-Hit Number
skills.piloting: Affects movement and physical attacks — higher Piloting skill reduces movement penalties and improves physical attack accuracy

green.description: New recruits, prone to errors and may panic under fire

elite.description: Highly skilled warriors, can perform advanced maneuvers

ace.description: Legendary pilots, can turn the tide of battle

consciousness_and_wounds.description: When a MechWarrior takes damage (wounds), they must make a Consciousness Roll.
rules: Roll 2D6 and compare to the consciousness number
If the roll fails, the warrior is immediately knocked unconscious
An unconscious MechWarrior cannot control their mech
During the End Phase, roll 2D6 to attempt to recover
If the result meets or exceeds the consciousness number, the warrior regains consciousness
MechWarriors can survive up to 5 points of damage; beyond that, they die

lance.description: A Lance is the basic tactical unit in BattleTech, consisting of 4 BattleMechs.
lance.command: Lance Commander coordinates the actions of the individual MechWarriors

company.description: A Company consists of 10 Lances (40 BattleMechs).

fps_specific_rules.description: FPS-specific rules from MechWarrior video games.

cockpit_view.description: First-person cockpit view as the primary perspective. The player sees the BattleMech from inside the cockpit with instrument panels, targeting displays, and weapon status indicators.
cockpit_view.third_person: Third-person external view available in most games for tactical overview

control_modes.basic: Point and Shoot — simplified controls where the mech aims and fires automatically
control_modes.advanced: Independent control of the mech legs and torso, with the player controlling left leg, right leg, and torso twist separately
control_modes.torso_twist: Allows the upper body to rotate independently for aiming while moving

weapon_targeting.description: Crosshair-based targeting with weapon-specific targeting reticles.
weapon_targeting.weapon_grouping: Weapons can be assigned to groups that fire together or in sequence (chain fire)
weapon_targeting.alpha_strike: Fires all weapons simultaneously for maximum damage
weapon_targeting.chain_fire: Fires weapons in sequence to manage heat and cooldowns
weapon_targeting.cooldowns: Each weapon has a cooldown period after firing — ballistic weapons reload while energy weapons cool down

component_damage.description: Component-based damage with separate integrity for each part.

destruction_effects.arms: Ripped off, loss of weapons mounted on that arm
destruction_effects.head: Pilot may be killed

stability.description: Mechs are bipedal walkers that must maintain balance. Weapon impacts can destabilize a mech, causing it to be knocked down.
effects: Knocked down mechs are temporarily unable to move or fire effectively
Pilot may take damage when knocked down
Jump jets can affect stability on landing

called_shots.description: Target specific parts of an enemy mech for focused damage.
rules: Riskier than normal attacks
Can quickly disable key components
Precision Strike ability allows called shots on standing mechs
Essential for strategic combat

electronic_warfare.description: Electronic warfare adds a layer of tactical depth.
electronic_warfare.ecm: Electronic Countermeasures — disrupts enemy targeting and radar
electronic_warfare.active_probes: Longer radar range and faster target lock

multiplayer_modes.instant_action: Quick customized battles for testing loadouts

scenario_types.skirmish: Small-scale engagements between lances or companies
scenario_types.battle: Large-scale engagements between regiments or larger forces
scenario_types.raid: One side attempts to capture or destroy a specific objective
scenario_types.defense: One side defends a position against an attacking force
scenario_types.patrol: A force searches for and engages enemy units
